Reproducing Schiavo et al. (2020) from dandiset 000249 and its figshare recordings¶

Paper. Schiavo JK, Valtcheva S, Bair-Marshall CJ, Song SC, Martin KA, Froemke RC (2020). Innate and plastic mechanisms for maternal behaviour in auditory cortex. Nature 587, 426-431. doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2807-6. The claims file was written from the NIH author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC7677212), with its Methods and the Extended Data legends; this attempt read the same text.

Dandiset. DANDI:000249, version 0.230423.1416 (doi:10.48324/dandi.000249/0.230423.1416). The paper cites no DANDI version (its data statement points to a figshare DOI). This is the only published version, so it is pinned. The draft lists the same 777 assets and size; it was modified later (2024-05-18), and the analysis uses nothing that a draft could change.

What the dandiset holds. 777 NWB files of 54 mice, each holding one raw, unaligned two-photon movie (TwoPhotonSeries), the subject id, a session description that names the stimulus set (for example base_r1_pc1_71b_j6a_61f_002), and an experiment description that names the group. There are no ROIs, fluorescence traces, stimulus times, stimulus order or trial tables. The paper's behavioural assays, whole-cell recordings and vocalization recordings are not in the dandiset.

Data from elsewhere. The dandiset's metadata links the figshare collection doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5043830.v6 (the paper's own figshare DOI, 10.35092/yhjc.c.5037737, does not resolve). The claims file marks the whole-cell, slice and operant claims data: elsewhere, at the figshare articles it names, which are read here at their versions: in vivo whole-cell recordings of experienced (12611657 v3) and naive females (12613496 v2), slice recordings with repeated stimulation (12611522 v1), oxytocin slice recordings (12613811 v1), operant touch times (13056584 v1) and the operant task code (13054076 v1). The imaging items of the collection hold the same unaligned movies as TIFF files, with the same descriptions, and add nothing that the dandiset lacks.

Claims. Tested here: subject-group-link, fig1g-ipsc-depress-faster, fig1i-operant-prototypes, ed5b-press-count-unchanged, ed6ef-epsc-tuning, fig2h-epsc-enhanced-ev, fig2i-ipsc-weaker-nv, fig2j-ie-ratio-tracks-isi, fig2k-ipsc-exceeds-epsc-575 and ed9b-oxytocin-enhances-spiking. Blocked:

Claims Reason
fig1a-isi-distribution, fig1c-warm-vs-cold, fig1c-salient-isis-retrieved, fig1c-slow-and-single-not-retrieved, ed2a-dams-evs-similar, ed2b-latency-slow-longer, ed2d-ymaze-approach, fig4c-ch575-retrieve-slow, fig4d-actx-inhibition-blocks, ed8hi-single-syllables-not-learned, fig4e-ot-inhibition-deficits data missing: the vocalization recordings and the retrieval and y-maze behaviour are neither in the dandiset nor in the figshare collection
ed4d-response-tracks-isi-probability data missing: it needs the ISI distribution of fig1a (and the imaging responses, below)
ed3e, fig1f, ed6c, ed3k, ed3m, ed4c, ed4e, ed4g, fig2d, ed6d, fig2e, fig2f, ed7bc, fig3e, fig3h, ed8cd, fig4b, fig4g, fig4h, ed3bc (all imaging claims) metadata insufficient: the movies carry no stimulus times and no order of the calls within a recording, and no ROIs
fig3-retrieval-onset-range metadata insufficient: the start of cohousing is not recorded
ed6h-dams-evs-epsc-similar metadata insufficient: the whole-cell spreadsheets do not say which experienced cells come from dams

Two tested claims end blocked as methods_underspecified because the readings the claims file names give different outcomes (fig1i-operant-prototypes, ed5b-press-count-unchanged). The five in vivo whole-cell claims (ed6ef-epsc-tuning, fig2h-epsc-enhanced-ev, fig2i-ipsc-weaker-nv, fig2j-ie-ratio-tracks-isi, fig2k-ipsc-exceeds-epsc-575) end blocked as other: in the deposited recordings the current almost never follows the calls, so the Methods' inclusion rule leaves too few cells; their sections show what the measure gives on every listed cell.

Revision after the first verification. The call onset is now the start of the sound (the first, quiet syllable was missed before); the data check adds trial-averaged currents aligned to it and three more tests of whether the currents follow the calls; the in vivo claims add the expected-direction reading of the largest trials; the subject link reads the figshare item titles; the slice section checks the pulse times against the artefacts; the oxytocin section prints the spreadsheet labels and a second reading of the control window; the operant interval is taken where the times are printed at 0.1 ms; the movies are folded at trial periods.

Revision after the second verification. The data check lists and draws the files with a sweep-locked deflection, with the latency and sign of each, and folds one three-call movie of each of 38 subjects at multiples of the trial period. The wording on the in vivo currents and on the imaging call order follows these numbers.

Data check¶

The dandiset¶

Every NWB file of the pinned version is opened (streamed); the survey reads each file's groups, the movie's shape, type and rate, the descriptions, and the first and last frame (to compare recordings). Nothing else of the movies is read here.

Each file holds one movie and nothing else: no processing module (no ROIs or traces), no stimulus series and no intervals (trials). The movies are 256 x 256 pixels at 3.90625 Hz, which matches the Methods' 256 x 256 pixels at "4 Hz (0.26 s/frames)". Indicator and location are "unknown" in every file, although the experiment descriptions name the indicator class and the hemisphere.

Recordings deposited more than once¶

Exact copies would share a checksum. Copies under a new encoding would share their frame count and the sums of their first and last frames.

Is the timing of the calls recoverable from the movies?¶

The calls were "played in a pseudorandom order (repetition rate: 0.1 Hz)" (Methods). With no stimulus times, a test of any imaging claim would need the onset and the identity of each call from the movie itself. The spectrum of the movie (8 x 8 pixel blocks, each as dF/F, high-passed with a 20 s moving average) is shown for a prototype file, a morph file and a pure tone file.

In [5]:
from scipy.ndimage import uniform_filter1d

def block_spectrum(s3):
    import h5py, remfile
    with h5py.File(remfile.File(s3), "r") as f:
        x = f["acquisition/TwoPhotonSeries/data"][:].astype(np.float32)
        fs = float(f["acquisition/TwoPhotonSeries/starting_time"].attrs["rate"])
    b = x.reshape(len(x), 32, 8, 32, 8).mean(axis=(2, 4)).reshape(len(x), -1)
    b = (b - b.mean(0)) / b.mean(0)
    b = b - uniform_filter1d(b, int(20 * fs), axis=0)
    P = (np.abs(np.fft.rfft(b, axis=0)) ** 2).mean(axis=1)
    return np.fft.rfftfreq(len(b), 1 / fs), P

examples = ["sub-NV43/sub-NV43_ses-20171014T183731_ophys.nwb",   # pc1: three prototypes
            "sub-EV27/sub-EV27_ses-20170425T192357_ophys.nwb",  # morph set of 61f,
            "sub-NV33/sub-NV33_ses-20170711T155914_ophys.nwb"]   # pure tones
examples = [p for p in examples if p in set(files.path)] or files.path.iloc[:3].tolist()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3))
for p in examples:
    row = files[files.path == p].iloc[0]
    fr, P = block_spectrum(row.s3)
    sel = (fr > 0.05) & (fr < 1.0)
    rel = P[sel] / np.median(P[sel])
    near = (fr[sel] > 0.09) & (fr[sel] < 0.11)
    top = np.argsort(rel)[::-1][:3]
    print(f"{row.session_description}: power at 0.09-0.11 Hz {rel[near].max():.1f} x median; "
          f"largest peaks at {np.round(fr[sel][top], 3).tolist()} Hz ({np.round(rel[top], 1).tolist()} x median)")
    ax.semilogy(fr[sel], rel, label=row.session_description[:40])
ax.axvline(0.1, color="grey", lw=0.5)
ax.set_xlabel("frequency (Hz)"); ax.set_ylabel("power / median"); ax.legend(fontsize=7)
plt.show()

# A sharper test of the call timing: fold each pixel (2 x 2 binned, dF/F, high-passed with a 30 s
# moving average) at a trial period and measure how much of its variance the folded mean (20 phase
# bins per 10.24 s) explains; the mean of the 200 strongest pixels, over a grid of periods. A period
# at which stimuli recur stands above its neighbours. Folding at k periods tests whether the k calls
# of a file recur in a fixed cycle (as in the whole-cell playback), which would make each phase one
# call.
def pixel_movie(s3):
    import h5py, remfile
    with h5py.File(remfile.File(s3), "r") as f:
        x = f["acquisition/TwoPhotonSeries/data"][:].astype(np.float32)
        fs = float(f["acquisition/TwoPhotonSeries/starting_time"].attrs["rate"])
    n = len(x)
    b = x.reshape(n, 128, 2, 128, 2).mean(axis=(2, 4)).reshape(n, -1)
    del x
    b = (b - b.mean(0)) / b.mean(0)
    return b - uniform_filter1d(b, int(30 * fs), axis=0), fs

def fold_strengths(b, fs, periods, bins_per_10s=20, top=200):
    n, tvar, out = len(b), b.var(0), []
    for P in periods:
        nb = max(4, int(round(bins_per_10s * P / 10.24)))
        k = ((np.arange(n) / fs % P) / P * nb).astype(int)
        m = np.stack([b[k == i].mean(0) for i in range(nb)])
        out.append(np.sort(m.var(0) / tvar)[-top:].mean())
    return np.array(out)

grid = np.round(np.arange(4.5, 12.001, 0.02), 2)
for p in examples:
    row = files[files.path == p].iloc[0]
    b, fs = pixel_movie(row.s3)
    s = fold_strengths(b, fs, grid)
    top3 = np.argsort(s)[::-1][:3]
    print(f"{row.session_description}: median over 4.5-12 s {np.median(s):.4f}; strongest periods "
          f"{[(float(grid[i]), round(float(s[i]), 4)) for i in top3]}; at 10.00 s {s[np.argmin(abs(grid - 10))]:.4f}; "
          f"40 frames = {40 / fs:.2f} s, 20 frames = {20 / fs:.2f} s")
    if "tone" not in row.session_description:
        cyc = []
        for k in range(1, 7):
            P = 40 / fs * k
            near = fold_strengths(b, fs, [P + d for d in (-0.6, -0.4, -0.3, 0.3, 0.4, 0.6)]).mean()
            cyc.append(f"{k}x: {fold_strengths(b, fs, [P])[0]:.4f} (nearby {near:.4f})")
        print("   folding at k x 40 frames:", "; ".join(cyc))
    del b

# Is a three-call cycle present in other movies? One file of each subject with the three-call set
# 71b, j6a, 61f (1220 frames), the first by path: the fold strength at k x 40 frames minus the mean
# at the nearby periods, for k = 1 to 6. A fixed cycle of three calls would make the excess at 3 x
# stand above those at 2 x and 4 x in most files.
three = files[files.session_description.str.contains(r"_pc1_71b_?j6a_?61f_", case=False) & (files.n_frames == 1220)]
three = three.sort_values("path").groupby("subject_id").head(1)
def cycle_excess(row):
    b, fs = pixel_movie(row.s3)
    ex = []
    for k in range(1, 7):
        P = 40 / fs * k
        ex.append(fold_strengths(b, fs, [P])[0] - fold_strengths(b, fs, [P + d for d in (-0.6, -0.4, -0.3, 0.3, 0.4, 0.6)]).mean())
    return {"subject": row.subject_id, "session": row.session_description[:40], **{f"{k}x": e for k, e in zip(range(1, 7), ex)}}
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex_pool:
    ex_tab = pd.DataFrame(list(ex_pool.map(cycle_excess, [r for _, r in three.iterrows()])))
print(ex_tab.round(4).to_string(index=False))
kx = ["1x", "2x", "3x", "4x", "5x", "6x"]
print(f"\nFiles: {len(ex_tab)} of {three.subject_id.nunique()} subjects; excess at 1x (the trial period) above 0.005 in "
      f"{int((ex_tab['1x'] > 0.005).sum())}")
print("Median excess at each multiple:", ex_tab[kx].median().round(4).to_dict())
print("Files whose largest excess is at each multiple:", ex_tab[kx].idxmax(axis=1).value_counts().reindex(kx, fill_value=0).to_dict())
print("Files with the excess at 3x above both 2x and 4x:", int(((ex_tab["3x"] > ex_tab["2x"]) & (ex_tab["3x"] > ex_tab["4x"])).sum()),
      "of", len(ex_tab), "| at 2x above 1x and 3x:", int(((ex_tab["2x"] > ex_tab["1x"]) & (ex_tab["2x"] > ex_tab["3x"])).sum()),
      "| at 4x above 3x and 5x:", int(((ex_tab["4x"] > ex_tab["3x"]) & (ex_tab["4x"] > ex_tab["5x"])).sum()))

Median excess at each multiple: {'1x': 0.014299999922513962, '2x': 0.006800000090152025, '3x': 0.016300000250339508, '4x': 0.006399999838322401, '5x': 0.007000000216066837, '6x': 0.01209999993443489}
Files whose largest excess is at each multiple: {'1x': 8, '2x': 2, '3x': 18, '4x': 0, '5x': 2, '6x': 8}
Files with the excess at 3x above both 2x and 4x: 31 of 38 | at 2x above 1x and 3x: 2 | at 4x above 3x and 5x: 1

In the call files the power near 0.1 Hz (3.8 and 6.2 times the median) does not stand above the slower fluctuations (8.9 and 10.4 times the median at 0.06 to 0.07 Hz). Folding single pixels at a trial period finds the stimulus period: in both call files the strongest period between 4.5 and 12 s is 10.24 s, 40 frames (fold strength 0.067 and 0.035 against a median of 0.030 and 0.018 over the grid; 0.034 and 0.021 at 10.00 s), and in the tone file 10.24 s and 5.12 s (20 frames), the Methods' 0.2 Hz tone rate tied to the frame clock. So the phase of the trials could be recovered from a movie; 40 frames is 0.098 Hz, the Methods' "0.1 Hz" rounded. In the first three-call file, 3 x 40 frames exceeds the nearby periods by 0.050, against 0.033 at one period and 0.024 at two; in the five-stimulus morph file 5 x 40 frames exceeds them by 0.011, no more than other multiples. Over one three-call movie of each of 38 subjects (the table above), the excess at 3 x 40 frames is above those at 2 x and 4 x in 31 of 38 files (median excess 0.016 at 3 x against 0.007 and 0.006), and the largest of the six multiples in 18; at 2 x it stands above its neighbours in 2 files and at 4 x in 1. The trial period itself stands out (excess above 0.005) in 27 of 38. So in most three-call movies the trials appear to recur in a fixed cycle of three, although the Methods say the calls were played "in a pseudorandom order". The cycle gives each trial a position, but nothing in the files says which call is played at which position or on the first trial: the session descriptions name the calls of a file, and whether their listed order is the playback order cannot be checked. Every imaging claim needs responses assigned to named calls (and ROIs, which are not deposited), so all are blocked as metadata_insufficient.

The figshare recordings¶

The in vivo whole-cell articles list each cell, file, stimulus set, holding potential and notes in a spreadsheet. Each ABF file has the membrane current and a microphone channel (MIC) that records the played call, from which the call's onset, offset and ISI are measured per sweep.

# Do the currents follow the calls? Four checks, per cell and current (EPSC at -70 mV, IPSC at a
# depolarized potential), on the morph-set sweeps used below (main selection).
rng_check = np.random.default_rng(13)
# (1) The Methods' evoked measure (call window minus the 1 s before onset), signed in the expected
# direction (inward for EPSCs, outward for IPSCs), against zero over trials; the same for the
# earlier onset rule (first loud syllable) and for the sham measure (0.7 s before onset minus the
# 0.7 s before that), the same test with no call in the window.
rows = []
for name, meas in (("call window", "evoked"), ("call window, loud-syllable onset", "evoked_loud"),
                   ("sham, before the call", "sham")):
    _, raw = S.psc_table(iv_list, iv_sweeps, top_n=5, measure=meas)
    for (grp, cell, kind), d in raw.groupby(["group", "cell", "kind"]):
        tt = stats.ttest_1samp(d.directed, 0)
        rows.append({"window": name, "group": grp, "cell": cell, "kind": kind, "trials": len(d),
                     "mean directed pA": d.directed.mean(), "share expected sign": (d.directed > 0).mean(),
                     "p": tt.pvalue, "responds": bool(tt.statistic > 0 and tt.pvalue < 0.05)})
resp = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("(1) Cells whose mean evoked current over trials is in the expected direction at p < 0.05 (one test per cell;"
      " about 2.5% expected by chance):")
print(resp.groupby(["window", "kind", "group"]).responds.agg(["sum", "size"]).to_string())
print("Share of trials with the expected sign:", resp.groupby("window").apply(
    lambda d: round(np.average(d["share expected sign"], weights=d.trials), 3)).to_dict())
print("\nCall window, per cell:")
print(resp[resp.window == "call window"].drop(columns="window").round(3).to_string(index=False))

# (2) The response in the first 300 ms after onset, from the 5 ms binned traces, against the 300 ms
# before onset, in the expected direction.
_, raw_main = S.psc_table(iv_list, iv_sweeps, top_n=5)
tr = raw_main.merge(iv_sweeps[["file", "sweep", "trace"]], on=["file", "sweep"])
nb_pre = int(-S.TRACE_WIN_S[0] / S.TRACE_BIN_S)
b300 = int(0.3 / S.TRACE_BIN_S)
cell_traces, early = {}, []
for (grp, cell, kind), d in tr.groupby(["group", "cell", "kind"]):
    X = np.stack(d.trace.values).astype(float)
    X = (X - np.nanmean(X[:, nb_pre - b300:nb_pre], axis=1, keepdims=True)) * (-1 if kind == "EPSC" else 1)
    cell_traces[(grp, cell, kind)] = (X, d.isi.values)
    e = np.nanmean(X[:, nb_pre:nb_pre + b300], axis=1)
    tt = stats.ttest_1samp(e, 0)
    early.append({"group": grp, "cell": cell, "kind": kind, "trials": len(e), "0-300 ms, pA": e.mean(),
                  "p": tt.pvalue, "responds": bool(tt.statistic > 0 and tt.pvalue < 0.05)})
early = pd.DataFrame(early)
print("\n(2) Cells with a mean response in the expected direction 0-300 ms after onset at p < 0.05:")
print(early.groupby(["kind", "group"]).responds.agg(["sum", "size"]).to_string())
print("0-300 ms response (pA, expected direction), median and range over cells:",
      early.groupby("kind")["0-300 ms, pA"].agg(["median", "min", "max"]).round(2).to_dict("index"))

# (3) Any deflection locked to the sweep at any time from onset to 3 s after: per file, the largest
# |t| of the trial mean over 20 ms bins, against 200 random sign flips of the trials.
def max_t(Y):
    mu = np.nanmean(Y, 0); se = np.nanstd(Y, 0) / np.sqrt(len(Y))
    return np.nanmax(np.abs(mu / se))
scan, scan_curves = [], {}
sets_sw = iv_sweeps.merge(iv_list[["file", "group", "cell", "holding", "set"]], on="file").dropna(subset=["onset"])
for (grp, cell, f, hold, st), d in sets_sw.groupby(["group", "cell", "file", "holding", "set"]):
    if len(d) < 5:
        continue
    X = np.stack(d.trace.values).astype(float)
    X = X.reshape(len(X), -1, 4).mean(axis=2)                     # 20 ms bins
    pre = nb_pre // 4
    X = X[:, pre:] - np.nanmean(X[:, pre - 10:pre], axis=1, keepdims=True)
    obs = max_t(X)
    null = np.array([max_t(X * rng_check.choice([-1, 1], size=(len(X), 1))) for _ in range(200)])
    mu = np.nanmean(X, 0); tc = mu / (np.nanstd(X, 0) / np.sqrt(len(X)))
    j, sign = int(np.nanargmax(np.abs(tc))), (-1 if hold < -30 else 1)
    above = np.flatnonzero(np.abs(tc) > np.quantile(null, 0.95))
    scan.append({"group": grp, "cell": cell, "file": f, "kind": "EPSC" if hold < -30 else "IPSC",
                 "set": "5 prototypes" if "5xcalls" in st else "morph set", "sweeps": len(X),
                 "max |t|": obs, "p": float(np.mean(null >= obs)),
                 "peak s": (j + 0.5) * 0.02, "peak pA, expected direction": sign * mu[j],
                 "first bin above null s": (above[0] + 0.5) * 0.02 if len(above) else np.nan,
                 "bins above null": len(above)})
    scan_curves[f] = (sign * X, sign * mu, tc)
scan = pd.DataFrame(scan)
print("\n(3) Files with a sweep-locked deflection anywhere 0-3 s after onset at p < 0.05 (5% expected by chance):")
print(scan.groupby(["set", "kind"]).p.agg(n_files="size", significant=lambda p: int((p < 0.05).sum())).to_string())

# (4) The Methods' inclusion rule: at least five significant prototype-evoked PSCs, a significant PSC
# being a trial whose current in the expected direction exceeds k s.d. of the cell's sham measure.
# The same rule applied to the sham trials gives its false-positive rate.
incl_tabs = {}
for k in S.SIG_K:
    _, tab = S.significant_cells(iv_list, iv_sweeps, k)
    incl_tabs[k] = tab
    _, sh = S.psc_table(iv_list, iv_sweeps, measure="sham")
    sd_ = sh.groupby(["group", "cell", "kind"]).directed.transform("std")
    print(f"\n(4) k = {k}: share of call trials significant {tab.sig_share.mean():.3f} (mean over cells); "
          f"share of sham trials passing the same rule {(sh.directed > k * sd_).mean():.3f}")
    print("Cells with at least 5 significant prototype trials:")
    print(tab.groupby(["kind", "group"]).agg(cells=("included", "size"), included=("included", "sum"),
                                             max_sig_proto=("proto_sig", "max")).to_string())
    print("Included:", tab[tab.included].reset_index()[["group", "cell", "kind", "proto_sig"]].to_dict("records"))

sd = iv_sweeps.merge(iv_list[["file", "group", "holding"]], on="file").dropna(subset=["baseline_sd"])
sd["kind"] = np.where(sd.holding < -30, "EPSC", "IPSC")
print("\nBaseline current s.d. within a sweep (pA), median by group and current:")
print(sd.groupby(["kind", "group"]).baseline_sd.median().round(2).to_string())

# The files of check (3) with a sweep-locked deflection at p < 0.05: when the deflection peaks, its
# sign (positive is the expected direction, inward for EPSCs and outward for IPSCs), and the first
# 20 ms bin whose |t| exceeds the 95th percentile of the file's sign-flip null. A current that follows
# the calls would have a consistent latency after onset and the expected sign; chance deflections
# fall anywhere in the 3 s and in either direction.
print("Binomial p of the counts of check (3) against a rate of 0.05 (one-sided): all files %d of %d, p = %.4f; morph-set EPSC files %d of %d, p = %.4f"
      % ((scan.p < 0.05).sum(), len(scan), stats.binomtest(int((scan.p < 0.05).sum()), len(scan), 0.05, alternative="greater").pvalue,
         ((scan.p < 0.05) & (scan.set == "morph set") & (scan.kind == "EPSC")).sum(), ((scan.set == "morph set") & (scan.kind == "EPSC")).sum(),
         stats.binomtest(int(((scan.p < 0.05) & (scan.set == "morph set") & (scan.kind == "EPSC")).sum()),
                         int(((scan.set == "morph set") & (scan.kind == "EPSC")).sum()), 0.05, alternative="greater").pvalue))
sig13 = scan[scan.p < 0.05].sort_values(["group", "cell", "file"])
print(sig13.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("Of these, peaking in the expected direction:", int((sig13["peak pA, expected direction"] > 0).sum()),
      "| peaking within 1 s of onset in the expected direction:",
      int(((sig13["peak pA, expected direction"] > 0) & (sig13["peak s"] < 1)).sum()))
print("Peak time over all", len(scan), "files (s): quartiles", scan["peak s"].quantile([0.25, 0.5, 0.75]).round(2).tolist())

for ax, (_, r) in zip(axs.flat, sig13.iterrows()):

    ax.axhline(0, color="grey", lw=0.5); ax.axvline(r["peak s"], color="tab:red", lw=0.5)
    ax.set_title(f"{r.group[:3]} {r.cell} {r.file}\n{r.kind}, {r.set}", fontsize=7)

The microphone channel gives every sweep of the 82 complete morph-set files a call, and in each of them the four call durations fall in four separate groups that repeat in a fixed order (prototype, 125, 275, 575 ms); the median measured silent gaps of the four groups are 142, 192, 301 and 604 ms. The stimulus therefore follows the legends' ISIs (125, 175, 275, 575 ms), not the Methods' "125, 225, 575". The order is fixed, not pseudorandom. Playback starts at the same time in every sweep (1.519 to 1.577 s; within a file the onsets spread by 0.4 ms at the median). The first syllable of many calls is much quieter than the rest, and the onset of the first loud syllable, the rule used before revision, comes a median 193 ms (up to 644 ms) after the start of the call, more than 50 ms late in 51 of 83 files; the call onset is now the start of the sound, and the earlier rule is a variant. File 19424013 is listed at -70 mV but carries about +560 pA throughout, as recorded at a depolarized potential; 19411001 is listed at -70 mV and its note says "some sweeps are at positive potentials". Sweeps whose current contradicts the listed potential are dropped (the counts are printed above); keeping them is a variant below.

The recorded currents almost never follow the calls. (1) The Methods' evoked measure is in the expected direction at p < 0.05 in 2 of the 39 cell recordings (one naive EPSC cell, 190326_e1, and one experienced IPSC cell with 19 trials), against 3 of 39 for the same test before the call; 48% of trials have the expected sign, against 47% before the call. (2) No cell has a mean response in the first 300 ms after onset at p < 0.05 (cell means -4.2 to 4.1 pA for EPSCs), and the mean over cells is 0.25 pA for EPSCs and 0.21 pA for IPSCs. (3) 13 of 110 files have a sweep-locked deflection anywhere in the 3 s after onset at p < 0.05 against sign-flipped trials, more than the 5.5 expected by chance (binomial p = 0.0034; 9 of the 55 morph-set EPSC files, p = 0.0015), and only 1 of the 28 files of five prototypes, which were played to find each cell's best call. Listed and drawn, 3 of the 13 carry a current in the expected direction during the call: both EPSC files of naive cell 190326_e1 (peaks of 48 and 42 pA at 0.79 and 0.73 s; expected sign 0.4 to 1.2 s after onset in 13 of 15 and 34 of 40 trials) and one of the two EPSC files of experienced cell 190313_e2 (37 pA at 0.77 s, 25 of 31 trials). In all three the current first exceeds the file's null 0.39 to 0.51 s after the start of the sound, while the call lasts 0.8 to 1.1 s. This is a call-locked inward current with a consistent latency, which the 0-300 ms test of check (2) misses; because playback starts at the same time in every sweep, a current locked to the sweep cannot be told apart from one locked to the call. The other 10 files peak at scattered times (0.11 to 2.91 s after onset), 9 of them against the expected direction, and the tenth (19410006) peaks at 2.75 s, after the call has ended. (4) With a significant PSC defined as a trial beyond 2 s.d. of the cell's sham measure in the expected direction, 3.9% of call trials pass against 3.7% of sham trials, and 1 of 39 cell recordings has the five significant prototype trials the Methods require (none at 3 s.d.); that recording is 190326_e1, a naive cell. The figure draws every cell's trial means by ISI. The baseline current varies about twice as much in experienced as in naive recordings (s.d. 11.4 against 5.3 pA for EPSCs, 21.9 against 6.2 pA for IPSCs).

op["first_s"] = op.touches.map(lambda v: v.min() if len(v) else np.nan)
op["last_s"] = op.touches.map(lambda v: v.max() if len(v) else np.nan)
op["interval_ms"] = op.touches.map(S.sampling_interval) * 1000
print("Operant files:", len(op), "| mice per group:", op.groupby("group").mouse.nunique().to_dict(), "(paper: 7 per group)")
print("Sessions per mouse:", op.groupby("mouse").session.nunique().value_counts().to_dict(),
      "| missing sessions:", {m: sorted(set(range(1, 9)) - set(g.session)) for m, g in op.groupby("mouse") if set(range(1, 9)) - set(g.session)})
print("Part b files joined to their session:", op[op.part_b].name.tolist())
print("Touch times (s): first %.2f to %.2f, last %.1f to %.1f (sessions run 1800 s after a start offset)"
      % (op.first_s.min(), op.first_s.max(), op.last_s.min(), op.last_s.max()))
print("Median interval between touch samples per session (ms, from times below 10 s, printed at 0.1 ms): median %.2f, range %.2f-%.2f, over %d sessions with such times"
      % (op.interval_ms.median(), op.interval_ms.min(), op.interval_ms.max(), op.interval_ms.notna().sum()))
allt = np.concatenate(op.touches.values)
for lo, hi in [(0, 10), (10, 100), (100, 1000), (1000, 3000)]:
    v = allt[(allt >= lo) & (allt < hi)]
    d = np.diff(np.unique(v))
    print(f"times {lo}-{hi} s: smallest step between distinct values {d.min():.4f} s; "
          f"share of samples repeating the previous value {np.mean(np.diff(v) == 0):.2f}")

times 1000-3000 s: smallest step between distinct values 0.1000 s; share of samples repeating the previous value 0.99

The touch times are printed with five significant digits (MATLAB dlmwrite's default), so they step by 0.1 ms below 10 s, 1 ms to 100 s, 10 ms to 1000 s and 100 ms after that, and most samples after 100 s repeat the value before them. A press can only be resolved to that step: a gap must exceed one and a half local steps to end a press (the helper's presses, which takes 1 ms as the step below 100 s). Where the times are printed at 0.1 ms, the task code polls the sensor every 0.70 ms at the median (0.50 to 0.80 ms over the 31 sessions with touches before 10 s).

subject-group-link¶

The dandiset's subjects can be assigned to the paper's imaging groups (experienced or naive virgin, dam, right cortex, cohousing, CH+575, opto-OT; excitatory, inhibitory or pan-neuronal indicator), with stimulus identity (prototype or morph ISI) for each presentation.

Result: partially reproduced. Every subject has a figshare item titled with its mouse id, and the titles agree with the experiment descriptions on experience group (49 of 49 where the description gives one), cell class (54 of 54) and right hemisphere (54 of 54). The five mice imaged only with tones take their group from the titles: EV56 and EV62 experienced (their descriptions call them NV56 and NV62), NV64, NV66 and NV140 naive. The counts match the paper for EV excitatory in left cortex (9), EV interneurons (5), EV right cortex (4), the dam (1), CH+575 (6), CH+575 opto-OT (4) and naive interneurons (6). 14 subjects have a first retrieval session, against the paper's 13 chronically imaged virgins, and 23 naive excitatory mice of several kinds stand against the 12 of Fig. 1f, which the paper does not name. No file holds a stimulus series or a trial table, so no presentation can be assigned its call or ISI, which the criterion makes a partial result. Three recordings are deposited under both NV58 and NV63.

fig1g-ipsc-depress-faster¶

In pup-naive auditory cortical slices, IPSCs depress faster than EPSCs at the prototypical stimulation rate (175 ms), while EPSCs and IPSCs depress similarly at 75 or 575 ms.

Method from the Methods ("The peak amplitude of evoked EPSCs and IPSCs were measured and normalized to the event evoked by the first stimulation on each trial (Sn/S1)") and the claims file: per cell the mean Sn/S1 over trials; IPSC against EPSC by one-way ANOVA (with two groups the same test as an unpaired t-test) under reading (a), per pulse with Bonferroni over pulses 2 to 5, and (b), the mean over pulses 2 to 5. The peak is the largest inward (EPSC) or outward (IPSC) current 2 to 30 ms after each pulse against the 5 ms before it, a standard choice stated in the helper. A trial whose first IPSC or EPSC is not above baseline gives no ratio and is dropped; the mean trace of each file is a variant.

In [17]:
def stp_tests(amps, label):
    a = amps.pivot_table(index=["rate", "cell", "kind", "file", "sweep"], columns="pulse", values="amp")
    dropped = int((a[1] <= 0).sum())
    a = a[a[1] > 0]
    c = a.div(a[1], axis=0).groupby(["rate", "cell", "kind"]).mean()
    rows = []
    for rate in (75, 175, 575):
        e = c.xs((rate, "EPSC"), level=("rate", "kind"))
        i = c.xs((rate, "IPSC"), level=("rate", "kind"))
        p = np.array([stats.ttest_ind(i[k], e[k]).pvalue for k in (2, 3, 4, 5)])
        mi, me = i[[2, 3, 4, 5]].mean(axis=1), e[[2, 3, 4, 5]].mean(axis=1)
        rows.append({"variant": label, "rate": rate, "n_E": len(e), "n_I": len(i),
                     "E_S2..S5": e[[2, 3, 4, 5]].mean().round(2).tolist(), "I_S2..S5": i[[2, 3, 4, 5]].mean().round(2).tolist(),
                     "(a) p per pulse, Bonferroni": np.round(np.minimum(p * 4, 1), 3).tolist(),
                     "(a) I below E at p<0.05": bool(((p * 4) < 0.05).any() and (i[[2, 3, 4, 5]].mean() < e[[2, 3, 4, 5]].mean())[(p * 4) < 0.05].all()),
                     "(b) mean S2-5 E": round(me.mean(), 2), "(b) mean S2-5 I": round(mi.mean(), 2),
                     "(b) p": round(stats.ttest_ind(mi, me).pvalue, 4),
                     "(b) paired p": round(stats.ttest_rel(mi.loc[mi.index.intersection(me.index)], me.loc[mi.index.intersection(me.index)]).pvalue, 4)})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows), dropped

t1, d1 = stp_tests(sl_amps[sl_amps.sweep >= 0], "per trial")
t2, d2 = stp_tests(sl_amps[sl_amps.sweep < 0], "mean trace per file")
print(f"Trials dropped for a first response not above baseline: {d1} (per trial); files dropped: {d2} (mean trace)")
print(pd.concat([t1, t2]).to_string(index=False))

# Do the pulse times from the protocol fall on the stimulus artefacts? For the first sweep of every
# slice file, the time of the steepest current change within 5 ms of each computed pulse time,
# relative to it; and one sweep drawn with the pulse times, baseline and peak windows.
def artefact_offsets(f):
    abf = S.abf_from_bytes(S.fetch(sl_files[f + ".abf"]["download_url"]), f + ".abf")
    fs = abf.dataRate
    abf.setSweep(0)
    y = abf.sweepY.copy()
    out = []
    for start, per, n, level in S.pulse_trains(abf):
        for k in range(n):
            tp = start + k * per
            a, b = tp - int(0.005 * fs), tp + int(0.005 * fs)
            out.append({"file": f, "level": level, "pulse": k + 1,
                        "offset_ms": (a + np.argmax(np.abs(np.diff(y[a:b + 1]))) - tp) / fs * 1000})
    return out
with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    art = pd.DataFrame(sum(ex.map(artefact_offsets, sl_list[sl_list.on_figshare].file), []))
print("Steepest change relative to the computed pulse time (ms), over", art.file.nunique(), "files and", len(art), "pulses:")
print(art.offset_ms.describe().round(3).to_string())
print("Pulses whose steepest change is within 1 ms of the computed time: %.1f%%" % (100 * (art.offset_ms.abs() <= 1).mean()))

for ax, (start, per, n, level) in zip(np.atleast_1d(axs), trains):
    i0, i1 = start - int(0.05 * fs), start + n * per + int(0.05 * fs)
    tt = np.arange(i0, i1) / fs * 1000
    ax.plot(tt, y[i0:i1], color="k", lw=0.5)

        ax.axvline(tp / fs * 1000, color="r", lw=0.5)
        ax.axvspan((tp - S.SLICE_BASE_S * fs) / fs * 1000, tp / fs * 1000, color="b", alpha=0.2)
        ax.axvspan((tp + S.SLICE_PEAK_WIN_S[0] * fs) / fs * 1000,

    lo, hi = np.percentile(y[i0:i1], [0.5, 99.5])
    ax.set_ylim(lo - 0.2 * (hi - lo), hi + 0.2 * (hi - lo))
    ax.set_title(f"{f}, held at {level:g} mV", fontsize=9); ax.set_xlabel("ms from sweep start")

          f"axis clipped to {lo - 0.2 * (hi - lo):.0f} to {hi + 0.2 * (hi - lo):.0f} pA (artefact peaks fall outside)")

Result: not reproduced. At 175 ms IPSCs do not depress more than EPSCs. Per trial, the mean Sn/S1 over pulses 2 to 5 is 0.90 for IPSCs against 0.68 for EPSCs (p = 0.33), and no pulse differs after Bonferroni correction (all adjusted p = 1.0). On the mean trace of each file the IPSC ratio is lower (0.57 against 0.65, p = 0.39), with pulses 2 and 3 at adjusted p 0.15 and 0.06. At 75 ms neither reading differs (p 0.52 and 0.72 for the mean over pulses). At 575 ms the unpaired tests do not differ (p 0.08 and 0.82), but on mean traces the paired test finds IPSCs lower than EPSCs (0.55 against 0.66, p = 0.022), where the claim has them similar. 35 trials and 7 file means with no first response above baseline were dropped, and 17 cell means of Sn/S1 fall outside 0 to 2, so the per-trial IPSC ratios are noisy. The outcome rests on the peak measure (2 to 30 ms after each pulse against the 5 ms before it), which the paper does not specify. The pulse times read from the protocol fall on the stimulus artefacts: the steepest change of the current is a median 0.5 ms after the computed time, within 1 ms for 91.8% of 740 pulses, and the drawn sweep shows the windows. Per trial and on mean traces the IPSC ratio at 175 ms moves in opposite directions (0.90 and 0.57 against 0.68 and 0.65 for EPSCs); the single-trial ratios are noisy (cell means of Sn/S1 range from -1.29 to 4.34), and neither direction is significant.

fig1i-operant-prototypes¶

Of naive virgins able to silence playback with a lever press, only those hearing prototypes significantly increased their press duration by session 8.

The claims file's readings: a press ends at a gap above (a) twice the median inter-sample interval or (b) 100 ms; the comparison is (a) session 1 against session 8, or (b) the mean of sessions 1-2 against 7-8; paired two-tailed t-test per group of 7 mice. Files marked b are joined to their session. The median inter-sample interval is the polling period of the task code, so it is taken once, pooled over sessions, from the touch times printed at 0.1 ms (below 10 s; data check): 0.70 ms. Above 10 s the printed times step by 1 ms or more, and the median of the printed intervals there (1.0 ms) would measure the printing, not the polling. Because a gap must also exceed one and a half printed steps, the gap that ends a press grows with time in the session (printed below): under the median-interval rule 1.5 ms before 100 s, 15 ms to 1000 s and 150 ms after, so a 50 ms pause splits a press early in a session but not after 1000 s.

In [20]:
glob_interval = float(np.median(np.concatenate(op.touches.map(S.interval_samples).values)))
print("Median interval between touch samples, pooled over sessions (from times below 10 s, printed at 0.1 ms): %.2f ms"
      % (1000 * glob_interval))
print("Smallest gap that ends a press (ms), by time in the session (the printed step sets a floor):")
for lo, mid in ((0, 5.0), (10, 50.0), (100, 500.0), (1000, 1500.0)):
    print(f"  from {lo} s: median2 rule {1000 * max(2 * glob_interval, 1.5 * float(S.resolution(mid))):.1f}, "
          f"100 ms rule {1000 * max(0.1, 1.5 * float(S.resolution(mid))):.0f}")
rows = []
for (mouse, grp, ses), d in op.groupby(["mouse", "group", "session"]):
    t = np.concatenate(d.touches.values)
    iv = glob_interval
    for rule in ("median2", "100ms"):
        p = S.presses(t, rule, iv)
        rows.append({"mouse": mouse, "group": grp, "session": ses, "rule": rule, "presses": len(p),
                     "mean_duration_s": p[:, 2].mean() if len(p) else np.nan, "max_duration_s": p[:, 2].max() if len(p) else np.nan})
press = pd.DataFrame(rows)

def operant_tests(measure):
    out = []
    for rule in ("median2", "100ms"):
        for comp in ("1 vs 8", "1-2 vs 7-8"):
            for grp in ("proto", "fast", "slow"):
                x = press[(press.rule == rule) & (press.group == grp)].pivot(index="mouse", columns="session", values=measure)
                a, b = (x[1], x[8]) if comp == "1 vs 8" else (x[[1, 2]].mean(axis=1), x[[7, 8]].mean(axis=1))
                ok = a.notna() & b.notna()
                tt = stats.ttest_rel(b[ok], a[ok])
                out.append({"gap rule": rule, "comparison": comp, "group": grp, "n": int(ok.sum()),
                            "early": round(a[ok].mean(), 3), "late": round(b[ok].mean(), 3),
                            "t": round(tt.statistic, 2), "p": round(tt.pvalue, 4),
                            "increase at p<0.05": bool(tt.pvalue < 0.05 and tt.statistic > 0)})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

dur = operant_tests("mean_duration_s")
print("\nMean press duration, session comparisons (paired two-tailed t-test):")
print(dur.to_string(index=False))
verdict = dur.groupby(["gap rule", "comparison"]).apply(
    lambda d: bool(d.set_index("group").loc["proto", "increase at p<0.05"]
                   and not d.set_index("group").loc[["fast", "slow"], "p"].lt(0.05).any()))
print("\nReading reproduces the claim (prototypes increase, the others not significant):")
print(verdict.to_string())

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). Prototypes increase the mean press duration under all four readings (session 1 against 8: p = 0.025 with the median-interval gap, 0.0076 with the 100 ms gap; sessions 1-2 against 7-8: p = 0.032 and 0.021). The fast and slow groups are not significant under three readings (p 0.081 to 0.73), but with the 100 ms gap and session 1 against 8 the slow group also increases (p = 0.040) and the fast group reaches p = 0.050. The criterion blocks the claim when the readings disagree. The reading closest to the paper's p-values (0.03, 0.24, 0.13) is the median-interval gap with session 1 against 8 (0.025, 0.081, 0.17). The press-ending gap of the median-interval rule depends on when in the session a press falls (1.5 to 150 ms), a consequence of the printed resolution that no reading avoids.

ed6ef-epsc-tuning¶

In experienced females, prototype- and morph-evoked EPSCs are similar and negatively correlated with ISI; in naive cortex morph-evoked EPSCs are weaker than prototype-evoked ones and uncorrelated with ISI.

Method (Methods, "In vivo whole-cell recordings", quoted in the helper): per sweep the mean current from call onset to 250 ms after call offset minus the mean of the 1 s before onset; per cell and ISI the mean absolute value of the largest 5 or 10 trials (both run). EPSCs are the files held at -70 mV, IPSCs those at 0 to +60 mV. Experienced cells pool dams and EVs (the spreadsheet does not separate them). Repeated-measures one-way ANOVA over the four ISIs; post hoc paired t-tests with Bonferroni correction, over the three comparisons with the prototype that the legend reports, and over all six pairs (a reading of the family, which the legend does not give). Pearson correlation over all cell and ISI points. The main analysis follows the spreadsheet notes and the best call where one is named, and drops sweeps whose holding current contradicts the listed potential. Variants: every sweep of every set file; the largest trials in the expected direction (inward for EPSCs, outward for IPSCs) instead of the largest absolute values, a second reading of "absolute magnitudes (pA) from the largest 5-10 evoked trials"; and the call onset taken at the first loud syllable, the rule used before revision. The Methods' inclusion rule ("Only neurons that exhibited at least five significant prototype-evoked E/IPSCs") leaves too few cells to run (data check), so every listed cell is used, and the numbers below measure the recordings, not call-evoked currents.

In [22]:
VARIANTS = {"main": {},
            "all sweeps": dict(apply_notes=False, best_call_only=False, check_holding=False),
            "expected direction": dict(select="expected"),
            "loud-syllable onset": dict(measure="evoked_loud")}

def psc(top_n, variant):
    t, raw = S.psc_table(iv_list, iv_sweeps, top_n=top_n, **VARIANTS[variant])
    return t.pivot_table(index=["group", "cell", "kind"], columns="isi", values="value"), t, raw

tables = {(n, v): psc(n, v) for n in S.TOP_N for v in VARIANTS}
w, t, raw = tables[(5, "main")]
print("Trials per cell and ISI (main, EPSC): min", int(t[t.kind == "EPSC"].n_trials.min()),
      "median", int(t[t.kind == "EPSC"].n_trials.median()))
print("Share of trials whose evoked current has the expected sign (EPSC inward, IPSC outward):",
      raw.assign(ok=lambda d: np.where(d.kind == "EPSC", d.evoked < 0, d.evoked > 0)).groupby("kind").ok.mean().round(2).to_dict())
print("Cells kept by the Methods' inclusion rule (data check):",
      {k: incl_tabs[k].groupby(["kind", "group"]).included.sum().to_dict() for k in S.SIG_K},
      "so the claims cannot be run on included cells; every listed cell is used below.")
rows = []
for (n, v), (w, _, _) in tables.items():
    for grp in ("experienced", "naive"):
        e = w.xs((grp, "EPSC"), level=("group", "kind")).dropna()
        long = e.reset_index().melt(id_vars="cell", var_name="isi", value_name="v")
        an = AnovaRM(long, "v", "cell", within=["isi"]).fit().anova_table
        p3 = {c: min(1, stats.ttest_rel(e[175], e[c]).pvalue * 3) for c in (125, 275, 575)}
        p6 = {(a, b): min(1, stats.ttest_rel(e[a], e[b]).pvalue * 6) for i, a in enumerate(e.columns) for b in e.columns[i + 1:]}
        r = stats.pearsonr(long.isi.astype(float), long.v)
        rows.append({"top": n, "variant": v, "group": grp, "cells": len(e),
                     "mean 125/175/275/575": e.mean().round(1).tolist(),
                     "RM ANOVA F": round(an["F Value"].iloc[0], 2), "RM p": round(an["Pr > F"].iloc[0], 4),
                     "175 vs 125/275/575, Bonf x3": [round(v_, 3) for v_ in p3.values()],
                     "smallest pair p, Bonf x6": round(min(p6.values()), 3),
                     "Pearson r": round(r.statistic, 3), "r p": round(r.pvalue, 4), "points": len(long)})
ed6ef = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(ed6ef.to_string(index=False))

Result: blocked (other). The current almost never follows the calls (data check): 2 of 39 cell recordings respond at p < 0.05 to the calls, against 3 of 39 before the calls; two cells (naive 190326_e1 and experienced 190313_e2, in one of its two files) carry an inward current during the call from about 0.4 s after onset; and the Methods' inclusion rule keeps 1 of 39 (2 s.d.) or none (3 s.d.), so the claim cannot be tested on the cells it is about. As computed on every listed cell it would not be reproduced: with the largest 5 trials, naive prototype-evoked EPSCs (20.0 pA) are not larger than morph-evoked ones (17.4, 18.3, 16.2 pA; adjusted p 0.12, 0.94, 0.20; repeated-measures ANOVA p = 0.18), and no variant gives p < 0.05 for all three comparisons (the expected-direction reading gives 0.034 at 575 ms only). Experienced EPSCs are not correlated with ISI (r = -0.14, p = 0.35; -0.09 to -0.21, p >= 0.16, under every variant). No experienced pair differs (smallest adjusted p 0.30 to 1.0) and the naive correlation is not significant (r = -0.07, p = 0.61), as in the paper.

Experienced EPSCs exceed naive ones at 125, 275 and 575 ms (one-tailed p 0.0023, 0.0062 and 0.0047 with the largest 5 trials) but also at the prototype (33.5 against 20.0 pA, p = 0.013; 0.0051 to 0.041 under every variant), where the claim has them similar. The same measure taken in the 0.7 s before the call gives the same group difference at every ISI (EV 32.0 to 35.7 against NV 14.8 to 19.6 pA, one-tailed p 0.0002 to 0.0047; ranking trials in the expected direction, p below 0.0001 to 0.023), as the baseline s.d. is about twice as large in experienced recordings. The difference is present before any call.

Result: blocked (other), as ed6ef-epsc-tuning: the current almost never follows the calls. As computed, the readings disagree. Experienced IPSCs exceed naive ones at 125, 275 and 575 ms under every variant (two-tailed p 0.0018 to 0.024). At 175 ms they do with the largest 10 trials (p 0.012 to 0.040) and with the expected-direction ranking (p = 0.021) but not with the largest 5 absolute values (p = 0.055, and 0.061 with the loud-syllable onset). Neither group's IPSC is correlated with ISI (r -0.19 to 0.13, p >= 0.347), as the claim says. The same measure taken before the call shows the same group difference (EV 31.9 to 45.9 against NV 12.8 to 13.8 pA, two-tailed p 0.0018 to 0.038; printed under fig2h). Seven experienced cells have IPSC recordings, where the paper has six; one of them (190410_e1) has only 4 or 5 trials per ISI, from one file of 19 sweeps, which may be the cell the paper left out, but the spreadsheet does not say so.

ed9b-oxytocin-enhances-spiking¶

Oxytocin enhances spiking to repeated 575 ms pulses in auditory cortical slices from stimulus 2 on, while stimulation without oxytocin does not change spike probability.

Spike probability per pulse (a crossing of 0 mV before the next pulse, a standard choice) at baseline (the files labelled baseline or PRE) and over the sweeps 15 to 30 minutes after wash onset (Methods), the onset being the first sweep of the first "wash in" file; for ACSF controls, "following baseline acquisition" (Methods) is read as from the first sweep after the baseline files. Friedman test over the ten columns (baseline and post for each stimulus) with Dunn's comparisons of baseline against post for each stimulus, Bonferroni over the five (the legend gives one p per stimulus); all 45 pairs and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests are variants.

In [28]:
stims = [f"stim{k}" for k in range(1, 6)]

def ox_table(control_anchor):
    """Baseline and 15-30 min post spike probability per cell. For controls the window counts from
    the first sweep after the baseline files ("after baseline", main) or from the first baseline
    sweep ("baseline start", a second reading of "following baseline acquisition")."""
    rows = []
    for (grp, cell), d in ox_sp.groupby(["group", "cell"]):
        d = d.sort_values("abs_t")
        base = d[d.role == "baseline"]
        if not len(base):
            base = d[d.file == d.file.iloc[0]]
        if grp == "oxytocin":
            onset = d[d.role == "wash in"].abs_t.min()
        elif control_anchor == "after baseline":
            onset = d[~d.file.isin(base.file)].abs_t.min()
        else:
            onset = base.abs_t.min()
        mins = (d.abs_t - onset).dt.total_seconds() / 60
        post = d[(mins >= S.OXY_WINDOW_MIN[0]) & (mins <= S.OXY_WINDOW_MIN[1]) & ~d.file.isin(base.file)]
        r = {"group": grp, "cell": cell, "baseline sweeps": len(base), "post sweeps": len(post),
             "post files": ",".join(sorted(post.file.unique()))}
        for s in stims:
            r["base " + s] = base[s].mean()
            r["post " + s] = post[s].mean() if len(post) else np.nan
        rows.append(r)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def ox_tests(ox, grp):
    x = ox[ox.group == grp].dropna(subset=["post stim1"])
    data = np.c_[x[["base " + s for s in stims]].values, x[["post " + s for s in stims]].values]
    chi, dunn = S.dunn_friedman(data, [(k, k + 5) for k in range(5)])
    _, dunn45 = S.dunn_friedman(data, [(i, j) for i in range(10) for j in range(i + 1, 10)])
    sel45 = dunn45.set_index("pair").loc[[(k, k + 5) for k in range(5)]]
    print(f"\n{grp}: {len(x)} cells with sweeps in the window (of {ox[ox.group == grp].shape[0]}); "
          f"Friedman chi2 = {chi.statistic:.2f}, p = {chi.pvalue:.2g}")
    out = pd.DataFrame({"stim": stims, "baseline": x[["base " + s for s in stims]].mean().values.round(3),
                        "post": x[["post " + s for s in stims]].mean().values.round(3),
                        "Dunn p, Bonf x5": dunn.p_bonf.round(4).values,
                        "Dunn p, Bonf x45": (sel45.p * 45).clip(upper=1).round(4).values,
                        "Wilcoxon p": [round(stats.wilcoxon(x["post " + s], x["base " + s]).pvalue, 4)
                                       if (x["post " + s] != x["base " + s]).any() else 1.0 for s in stims]})
    print(out.to_string(index=False))

ox = ox_table("after baseline")
print(ox.round(2).to_string(index=False))
for grp in ("oxytocin", "control"):
    ox_tests(ox, grp)
print("\nVariant: control window counted from the first baseline sweep")
ox_b = ox_table("baseline start")
print(ox_b[ox_b.group == "control"][["cell", "baseline sweeps", "post sweeps", "post files"]].to_string(index=False))

Result: reproduced, resting on the reading of the Dunn comparisons. In the 9 oxytocin cells spike probability rises from 0.035 to 0.051 at baseline to 0.48 to 0.56 in the 15 to 30 minutes after wash onset (Friedman chi2 = 51.35, p = 6e-08). With Dunn's comparisons of baseline against post for each stimulus, Bonferroni over five, stimuli 2 to 5 increase (adjusted p 0.022, 0.014, 0.0011 and 0.020) and stimulus 1 does not (p = 0.071), the pattern of the paper (0.34; 0.009, 0.008, 0.001, 0.04), although stimulus 1 also rises (0.044 to 0.48). The 5 ACSF controls with sweeps in the window show no change (Friedman p = 0.56, all adjusted p >= 0.79). The outcome depends on the comparison family: over all 45 pairs only stimulus 4 is significant (p = 0.0098), and Wilcoxon tests find stimulus 1 significant too (p = 0.0078). The label table shows each role: two controls (191202B and C) have one baseline file of 60 sweeps (0 to 11.8 min) and one later file (14.1 to 19.3 and 13.0 to 24.8 min), so the window 15 to 30 minutes after their first sweep after baseline holds no sweep. Counting the control window from the first baseline sweep instead brings in all 7 controls, which again show no change (Friedman p = 0.39, all adjusted p >= 0.47).

Blocked claims: what the data show¶

The start of cohousing is not recorded, so retrieval onset (fig3-retrieval-onset-range) cannot be measured. The hours from the last session imaged before the first retrieval session (a base, 24 or 48 hours PRE session) are printed with those from the last session named base. Either is an upper bound only if cohousing began after that session, which nothing in the files says; they are printed for the record and decide nothing. NV50 has no session named base, only a 24hrsPRE one.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. No claim on the dandiset's own data could be tested beyond the link: the movies carry no ROIs, stimulus order or stimulus times (the call period, 40 frames, can be found in the movies, and in 31 of 38 three-call movies a cycle of three trials, but not which call each trial played). The tested claims use the figshare recordings the claims file names. For the in vivo recordings the call's onset, timing and ISI come from the recorded microphone channel, and the stimulus sets hold the legends' ISIs (125, 175, 275, 575 ms). The recorded currents almost never follow the calls: 2 of 39 cell recordings respond to the calls on the Methods' measure, against 3 of 39 before the call; 13 of 110 files have a sweep-locked deflection, more than the 5.5 chance gives, but only two cells (190326_e1 and 190313_e2) carry a current in the expected direction during the call, from about 0.4 s after onset; and the Methods' inclusion rule, with a significant PSC defined here, keeps at most 1 of 39 cell recordings, so the five in vivo claims are blocked. Dams and EVs cannot be separated. Slice peaks are measured 2 to 30 ms after each pulse, a choice made here. Operant presses are reconstructed from touch times printed at a resolution of 0.1 to 100 ms. For the oxytocin slices the Dunn comparison family is read as five planned comparisons.

What was found about the dataset.

  • The dandiset holds only raw, unaligned two-photon movies. There are no ROIs or traces (the paper drew ROIs by hand), no stimulus times and no order of the calls within a recording, so none of the 20 imaging findings can be tested. The figshare imaging items hold the same movies as TIFF. The stimuli recur every 40 frames (10.24 s, the Methods' 0.1 Hz rounded; tones every 20 frames, 5.12 s). In 31 of 38 three-call movies the trials appear to recur in a fixed cycle of three, where the Methods say the order was pseudorandom; nothing says which call is at which position.
  • The behavioural data (retrieval, y-maze) and the vocalization recordings behind Fig. 1a are in neither the dandiset nor the figshare collection.
  • Three recordings are deposited under both NV58 and NV63, with the same start times and frames.
  • EV56 and EV62 are described as NV56 and NV62 in their files, and the five tones-only mice carry no experience group in their descriptions; the figshare item titles give it (EV56 and EV62 experienced, NV64, NV66 and NV140 naive). Indicator and location are "unknown" in every file, though the descriptions state both.
  • The paper's figshare DOI does not resolve; the dandiset links the figshare collection.
  • In the in vivo whole-cell data the current almost never follows the calls: two cells carry an inward current during the call from about 0.4 s after onset, and the rest show about as many responses as chance gives. The experienced recordings are about twice as noisy as the naive ones, and file 19424013 is listed at -70 mV but was recorded at a depolarized potential. The first syllable of many calls is much quieter than the rest. One listed file of each of the in vivo naive and slice articles is not on figshare. The spreadsheets do not mark dams.
  • The operant touch times are printed with five significant digits, so after 1000 s of a session they step by 0.1 s.
